page: Amazon Web Services r5b.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server offering direct physical access to dual Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture without a virtualization hypervisor overhead, it provides 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs at a 3.1 GHz clock frequency. The architecture is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 35 MB of L3 cache, hardware virtualization support (VMX), and advanced vector extensions including AVX-512.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory throughput. Multi-core evaluations such as stress-ng (81,986.24) and PassMark CPU (57,096.96) score in the top 25%, reinforced by an uncached large-block read memory bandwidth of 218.78 GB/sec. Application testing shows high capacity for memory-bound tasks, delivering 77.14 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and top-tier PassMark database operation scores. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1331.0) and single-threaded compression tests, rank in the middle 50%.

Hardware limitations reflect its specific profile: the instance has zero GPUs and provides no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning persistent disk storage relies strictly on network-attached configurations over its 25 Gbps baseline network link. Additionally, CPU-based large language model text generation rates fall within the bottom 10%, confirming it is not suited for generative AI inference.

From an efficiency standpoint, the bare-metal design eliminates hypervisor performance penalties and allocates massive physical DDR4 capacity. The r5b.metal instance is well matched for large in-memory databases, enterprise relational database systems, high-concurrency caching tiers, and multi-threaded compilation workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services r5b.metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processors. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) running at 3.1 GHz on an x86_64 architecture, paired with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory at an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network performance is anchored by a 25 Gbps baseline interface. The system lacks local disk storage and contains no discrete GPUs. Benchmarks highlight strong multi-core processing, exceptional memory bandwidth (218.78 GB/sec uncached reads), and superior throughput in in-memory workloads, demonstrated by 77.14 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core benchmarks rank average, and LLM text generation throughput is low. Without hypervisor overhead, r5b.metal fits large-scale relational databases, distributed caching systems, and heavy multi-threaded data processing.
